title: TEACHING EXAMPLE: kill 4 of 5 sealed mutants of a tally module, honestly
note: Worked example, NOT part of the benchmark. It mirrors the shape of the scored mutation cards (gc-348..gc-359, gc-422, gc-423, gc-428, gc-430) at miniature scale so you can see one full RED -> repair -> GREEN cycle without docker, without network, in a few seconds. Its reference solution ships in examples/mutation_testing/solution/; never publish solutions for the scored cards.
goal: assets/target/tally.py is a small normalise-and-count module and assets/mutants.jsonl seals 5 single-site mutants. Author a unittest suite under work/tests/ that stays green on the pristine module (>=6 tests) and goes RED on as many mutants as are actually killable. You must run the mutation loop yourself and file an honest work/kill_report.json naming exactly which mutant ids your suite kills: the sealed grader recomputes the kill set and disqualifies any over- OR under-claiming report. One mutant is semantics-preserving, so the ceiling is 4/5 -- reporting it as killed is a lie the grader catches. A green suite is not coverage evidence; only dead mutants are.
resources: Python >= 3.10 (stdlib only; no pip install, no network, no docker)
files under assets/ (target/tally.py, mutants.jsonl sealed mutant set, sealed grader grade.py)
process_expectations: work/plan.md (>=200 bytes) maps each observable behaviour of the module to an intended killer test before any test is written
baseline run on the pristine module actually executed and green before any mutant run
per-mutant verification loop actually ran; kill_report.json matches the recomputed kill set exactly (identities, not counts)
a surviving mutant triggers either another strengthen-and-re-run iteration or an explicit suspected-equivalent verdict with an argument -- never a report edit
sealed target and mutant list stay untouched (the grader hash-checks them)
